response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-12
CLINICAL INDICATION: Routine surveillance. History of treated breast cancer. No new symptoms.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. L. Okafor (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-02-10
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Differences from prior: the current image has slightly higher contrast and penetration, and breast shadows and left chest wall soft tissues lie differently.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F6, right hilum: right hilar and infrahilar fullness, indeterminate. The two reads did not agree. Not marked time-sensitive.
- F2, right lower zone: more conspicuous linear markings, indeterminate. Not marked time-sensitive.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central. Carina and main bronchi not narrowed. Lungs well inflated. No consolidation, mass or band-like collapse. Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. Coarse linear bronchovascular markings in the right medial lower zone are more conspicuous than on the prior, with no confluent consolidation (F2). This is indeterminate, because technique may account for the difference. A tiny dense focus projects over the right lower zone on the current; see CAN'T DETERMINE.
- Mediastinum / hila: Prominent aortic knuckle, consistent with an unfolded aorta, similar to prior (F3). Upper mediastinum not widened. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior (F6). This is indeterminate, and the two reads did not agree (only one of the two reads recorded it). The size change is not comparable between studies. The left hilum is not enlarged.
- Pleura: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax. Right costophrenic angle sharp. Left costophrenic angle appears sharp and is partly overlapped by breast shadow. No visible pleural thickening.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette within normal limits on PA, with clear borders, similar to prior (F4).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion seen at this resolution. Clavicles and shoulders intact. Mild curvature and degenerative change of the visible spine. Both breast shadows present. No soft tissue gas.
- Devices: Left chest wall implanted device with arcing tubing and a small metallic component over the left mid zone, consistent with an implanted venous access device (F1). It is present on both studies and stable, with no new device. The central catheter course and tip are not confidently traced.
- Below the diaphragm: Both domes well defined. More gas-filled bowel loops in the left upper abdomen on the current than on the prior (F5). This is indeterminate, and the two reads did not agree (only one of the two reads recorded it). No free gas under either dome.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Right hilar and infrahilar fullness, more conspicuous on the current (F6, indeterminate, reads disagreed). Right medial lower zone linear markings, more conspicuous on the current (F2, indeterminate). Tiny dense right lower zone focus on the current, not clearly visible on the prior. More left upper abdominal bowel gas on the current (F5, indeterminate, reads disagreed). The metallic component of the left chest wall device projects over a higher rib level on the current, and true migration cannot be judged.
- Unchanged: Left chest wall implanted venous access device present on both studies, with no new device (F1). Prominent aortic knuckle and upper mediastinal width (F3). Cardiac silhouette (F4). No pneumothorax.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed. No confirmed measurements.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on the current a true nodule, for example a calcified granuloma, or a vessel end-on? | Reason: The focus is very small, sits among crossing vessels, and is not clearly visible on the prior, which has lower contrast. A frontal film does not separate a small nodule from a vessel end-on or a bone island. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If it persists, CT chest.
- Is the increased conspicuity of the right lower zone markings a true interval change? (F2) | Reason: The current image has higher contrast and a different breast shadow position, both of which make markings look more prominent. | Recommend: Correlate clinically. Short-interval repeat PA and lateral, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Where is the catheter tip of the left chest wall device, and has the device moved? (F1) | Reason: The central course of the tubing is not traceable through the mediastinum at this resolution. The metallic component projects at a different rib level on the two films, which soft tissue and breast positioning might explain. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing for lines. Add a lateral view if tip position matters clinically.
- Is there a small left pleural effusion or a subtle left lower zone opacity? | Reason: Breast shadow overlaps the left costophrenic region and lower zone on both films, and there is no lateral view. | Recommend: Lateral view if clinically relevant.
- Are there subtle lesions in the ribs or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail such as pedicles and small lucent lesions is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.
- Is the right hilar and infrahilar fullness a real interval change, such as enlarged nodes or a hilar mass, or prominent vessels made more conspicuous by technique? (F6) | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessels from nodes or mass. The current is sharper and at deeper inspiration than the prior. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast. A lateral view would help if CT is not immediately available.
- Is the small dense nodular focus over the medial right lower zone on the current a true lung nodule, a calcified granuloma, or a vessel seen end-on? | Reason: It is a small focus on X-ray within crowded bronchovascular markings and breast shadow, and no definite matching focus is seen at the same site on the softer prior image. | Recommend: CT chest.
- Are the more conspicuous right lower zone linear markings a true interstitial change? (F2) | Reason: The current is sharper and slightly different in exposure and inspiration, and breast shadow overlies the region on both films. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If the difference persists there, CT chest.
- Where is the port catheter tip, and has the port or catheter moved? (F1) | Reason: The catheter tip cannot be traced over the mediastinum at this image resolution. The different projected level of the reservoir may reflect arm and breast position only. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing to trace the catheter to its tip. Add a lateral view if tip position remains unclear.
- Is the heterogeneous texture of the left humeral head a bone lesion or a normal or degenerative appearance? | Reason: The images are low resolution and the shoulder is at the edge of a chest film, so fine bone detail is unreliable. The appearance is similar on both studies. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the appearance persists.

IMPRESSION:
1. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior (F6). Indeterminate, and the two reads did not agree. A real change such as enlarged nodes or a hilar mass cannot be separated from prominent vessels made more conspicuous by technique. See CAN'T DETERMINE.
2. More conspicuous coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone (F2). Indeterminate, because technique may explain the difference. No confluent consolidation.
3. Tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on the current. Cannot be determined whether it is a nodule, a calcified granuloma or a vessel end-on.
4. Left chest wall implanted venous access device, present on both studies with no new device (F1). Catheter tip and any migration cannot be determined.
5. More left upper abdominal bowel gas on the current (F5). Indeterminate, and the two reads did not agree. No free gas under either dome.
6. No definite lung mass, confluent opacity, right pleural effusion or destructive rib lesion on the current PA film. Upper mediastinum not widened. Aortic knuckle and cardiac silhouette similar to prior. The left costophrenic region is partly hidden by breast shadow, and the left humeral head texture remains undetermined.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the right hilar and infrahilar fullness (F6). A lateral view would help if CT is not immediately available. No interval is specified in the findings.
- CT chest for the tiny dense right lower zone focus. First review the source images in PACS, and proceed to CT if it persists.
- For the right lower zone markings (F2): review the source images in PACS, and correlate clinically. If the difference persists, or there is clinical concern, obtain CT chest or a short-interval repeat PA and lateral. No interval is specified in the findings.
- Review the source images in PACS with line windowing to trace the catheter tip (F1). Add a lateral view if tip position matters clinically.
- Lateral view if clinically relevant, for the left costophrenic region hidden by breast shadow.
- Review the source images in PACS on bone settings for the ribs and spine. Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the left humeral head appearance persists.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
